WELCOME TO NEW MEMBERS 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, it gives me great pleasure to 
congratulate the newly elected/re-elected and nominated Members on 
behalf of this House and on my own behalf. I extend a very cordial 
welcome to all of them. Besides the Members who have made and 
subscribed oath or affirmation today, there are fifty-one Members who 
have already made and subscribed oath  or affirmation in my Chamber 
on the 3rd, 4th, 12th and 20th April 2006. 
Members, who are new to this House, I am sure, will soon 
acquaint themselves with the cont ents and contours of Parliamentary 
procedure and practice and use the same in enriching the proceedings 
of the House. We look forward to them for their valuable contribution in 
making the functioning of parliamentary democracy more effective and 
enhancing the dignity and prestige of this august House.

OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, I refer with profound 
sorrow to the passing away of Shrimati Sarla Bhadauria, Shri Bansi Lai 
and Dr. Shyam Sundar Mohapatra, former Members, and Shri Pramod 
Mahajan, a sitting Member of this House. 
Shrimati Sarla Bhadauria passed away on the 19 th March, 
2006, at the age of 86 years. 
Born at Dhamiapur village in Mai npuri district of Uttar Pradesh 
in 1921, Shrimati Bhadauria had her education at Wardha Ashram and 
Banaras Hindu College, Varanasi. 
An agriculturist by vocation, Shrimati Bhadauria participated in 
the freedom struggle and also suffered imprisonment. She was an 
active social worker and took keen interest in the cooperative 
movement and joint farming through modern methods. She devoted her 
life for the upliftment of the backward communities and eradication of 
untouchability. She worked for t he welfare of women and was 
associated with various ed ucational institutions. Till her last days, she 
took keen interest in the spread of education.  - 
Shrimati Bhadauria represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in 
this House from April, 1964 to April, 1970. 
In the passing away of Shrima ti Sarla Bhadauria the country 
has lost a devoted social worker. 
Shri Bansi Lai passed away on the 28 th March, 2006, at the 
age of 79 years following brief illness. 
Born at Golagarh village in Bh iwani District of Haryana, in 
August, 1927, Shri Bansi Lai had his education at Punjab University 
Law College, Jullundur. 
An agriculturist and an advocate, Shri Bansi Lai took keen 
interest in the co-operative move ment and the welfare of the deprived 
sections of society. He was Secretary, Praja Mandal, Loharu State 
from 1943 to 1944 and President of the Bar Association, Bhiwani, from 
1957 to 1958. Shri Bansi 
2

Lai was conferred the Honorary Degree of Doctor of Laws by the 
Kurukshetra University and Doctor  of Science by the Haryana 
Agricultural University in the year 1972. 
The long and illustrious legislativ e career of Shri Bansi Lai 
began in the year 1967, when he first got elected to the Haryana 
Legislative Assembly. He again got el ected to that Assembly in 1968, 
1972, 1986, 1991, 1996 and 2000. 
Shri Bansi Lai also had the unique distinction of serving as the 
Chief Minister of the State of Hary ana for three terms from May, 1968 
to November, 1975; June, 1986 to June 1987, and again from May, 
1996 to July, 1999. Under his stew ardship, the State made rapid 
strides in the fields of agriculture  and industry. He was considered as 
the architect of modern Haryana. 
Shri Bansi Lai represented the St ate of Punjab in this House 
from April, i960 to April, 1966 and the State of Haryana from April, 
1976 to January, 1980. He was also a Member of the Seventh, Eighth 
and the Ninth Lok Sabha. 
Shri Bansi Lai was Chairman of the Committee on Public 
Undertakings from 1980 to 1982 and the Estimates Committee from 
1982 to 
1984 of the Lok Sabha. 
Shri Bansi Lai also served as Minister in the Union Cabinet 
and held key portfolios like the Minister of Defence from December, 
1975 to March, 1977; the Minister of Railways from December, 1984 to 
September, 
1985 and the Minister of Transport from September, 1985 to June, 
1986. 
In the passing away of Shri Ba nsi Lai the country has lost a 
veteran Parliamentarian and an able administrator. 
Dr. Shyam Sundar Mohapatra passed away on the 22 nd April, 
2006, at the age of 78 years. 
Born at Balasore in Orissa in January, 1929, Dr. Mohapatra 
had his education at Balasore, Calcut ta University and University Law 
College, Calcutta. 
As a student leader, he organi sed student agitations and was 
arrested and imprisoned twice, first in 1946 and then in 1951. A 
multifaceted personality, Dr. Mohapatra  participated in the Quit India 
movement and other agitations against the British rule between 1942 
and 1947.   He took 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2006] 
keen interest in the social and cultural activities and organised many 
national level literary, cultural and musical conventions. Dr. Mohapatra 
was Chief Patron of many friendship societies with foreign countries. 
He was also President and Secretary of several Trade Union 
Organisations of Calcutta, Orissa, Mumbai and Delhi. 
Dr. Mohapatra was associated in different capacities with 
several dailies, weeklies and periodicals. He was recipient of the 
highest civil honour of the Argent ina Government for his work on 
International Understanding in the year 1983 and was conferred 
Honorary Diploma by the Argentina Council for Foreign Relations, the 
same year. He had proficiency in six languages and was a visiting 
Professor to Jamia Milia. He was also a visiting lecturer to many 
foreign educational institutions, societies and universities. 
The legislative career of Dr. Mohapatra commenced when he 
got elected to the Fifth Lok Sabha. He  represented the State of Orissa 
in this House from July, 1980 to July, 1986. 
A widely travelled person, Dr. Mohapatra, visited many 
countries. He visited Japan in 1982 as Guest of the Japanese Foreign 
Ministry. He had also visited China to discuss with the Chinese 
Leadership outstanding issues; visited Argentina as Guest of Argentina 
Government to deliver speeches in  Universities; visited the United 
States of America to lecture in the Woodrow Wilson Centre for 
International Scholars and Centre for Strategic and International 
Studies in George Town Universities; visited Nicaragua as Guest of the 
Government and organised a Medical Mission from India to Nicaragua 
and Venezuela to meet foreign policy experts. 
In the passing away of Dr. Shyam Sundar Mohapatra, the 
country has lost an able Parliamentarian, a noted trade unionist and a 
versatile personality. 
Shri Pramod Mahajan, passed away on the 3 rd May, 2006, at 
the age of 57 years, under tragic circumstances at the prime of his 
career. 
Born  at  Mahaboobnagar in Andhra Pradesh  in October,   
1949, Shri Mahajan had his education at  the Universities of Pune and 
Aurangabad. 
A social worker, Shri Mahajan started his career as a school 
teacher in the year 1971. He was General Secretary of the 
Maharashtra State Unit of the Bhar atiya Janata Party in the year 1978 
and went on to 
4 
 

[10 May, 2006]   RAJYA SABHA 
become Party's All India Secretary in 1983 and All India General   
Secretary from 1986 to 1987, 1992 to 1998 and again from 2003 till his 
sad demise. 
The illustrious and eventful legislat ive career of Shri Mahajan, 
which spanned over twenty years, started with the membership of 
Rajya Sabha in the year 1986. He represented the State of 
Maharashtra in this House for four terms from July, 1986 to July, 1992; 
from July, 1992 to May, 1996; from July, 1998 to July, 2004 and again 
from July, 2004 till he breathed his last. 
He was also elected to the Eleventh Lok Sabha. He was 
Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Transport and Tourism from April 1993 to March 1996. 
Shri Mahajan also served as Union Cabinet Minster and held 
the portfolios of Defence in the year 1996, Information and 
Broadcasting with additional charge of Food Processing Industries 
from December 1998 to October, 1999, Parliamentary Affairs from 
October 1999 to January 2003, with additional charge of Information 
Technology from November 1999 to January 2003, and 
Communications from September 2001 to January 2003. He also had 
the distinction of serving as Political Adviser to the then Prime Minister 
of India in the year 1998. 
An astute politician, Shri Mahajan carved out a niche for 
himself as a capable organiser who played an important role in the 
Indian political scene and in diverse sectors of national life with his 
innovative ideas. Shri Mahajan's ability in reaching out to the people, 
irrespective of their party affiliation, endeared him to one and all and 
this trait of his personality,  indeed, made him a successful 
Parliamentary Affairs Minister. 
Shri Mahajan was a powerful orator, not only in Hindi and 
English, but in Marathi as well. This House has, on several occasions, 
witnessed his oratorical skills. Whenever he rose in the House to 
speak on a matter or initiate a debate, the whole House listened to him 
with rapt attention. Ev erybody appreciated his or atorical skills and the 
conviction with which he advanced his arguments. Indeed, his 
contribution to the proceedings of  the House was always very 
valuable. 
From humble beginnings as a common man, his rise to a high 
position of eminence in public life with his dedication and sincere hard 
work will always be a source of inspiration for the young generation.

REFERENCES BY THE CHAIR 
The victims of fire at Victoria Park in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, it is with utmost grief and 
sorrow that I refer to the unfortunate incident of fire that took pla'ce at 
Victoria Park, Meerut, on the I0 lh April, 2006, thereby killing fifty-eight 
persons and injuring one hundred and sixty-two people. Three persons 
have also been reported missing. 
The loss of so many precious  lives has shocked the whole 
country. The loss suffered by the kith and kin of the deceased is 
irrepairable. Our hearts go out in sympathy for the bereaved families 
and we pray for the early   recovery   of   those   who   got   injured   in   
this   incident   of   fire. 
The killing of Shri K. Suryanarayan in Afghanistan 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, this House expresses its 
deep shock and profound grief over the killing of Shri K. Suryanarayan, 
an Indian Engineer, working in Afghanistan on April 29, 2006. 
The killing of an innocent individual working for the 
reconstruction and development of Afghanistan is a heinous crime and 
an inhuman act of terror. This House strongly condemns this barbaric 
act. This House calls on the Government of Islamic Republic of 
Afghanistan to apprehend and bring the perpetrators of this crime to 
justice. It expresses its solidarity with the

The victims of terrorist attacks in Jammu and Kashmir 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, as you are already 
aware thirty-two persons were killed and several others injured in two 
separate terrorist attacks in the Doda and Udhampur districts of the 
State of Jammu and Kashmir on the 30th April and 1st May, 2006. 
No words are strong enough to condemn this gruesome act 
of terrorism. The killing of so m any innocent perso ns has shocked 
the entire nation. I am sure that the whole House will join me in 
condemning this cowardly and senseless act and in offering 
condolences to the bereaved families and expressing concern and 
sympathy for those who got injured. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe 
silence as a mark of respect to t he memory of those who lost their 
lives.
